# Dimension: AI/LLM Integration

Reference file for [citations.md](../citations.md).

## AI Integration Approach

Hatchet is **not** an AI framework with native LLM nodes, embeddings, or RAG
primitives [1][17]. It is a general-purpose task orchestration platform that
positions AI agent workloads as a primary use case [1]. The value for AI is
durability, automatic retries, streaming, and distributed execution — not
AI-specific features.

"Hatchet is not opinionated on how you structure your LLM calls, business logic,
prompts, or context" — Icepick documentation [17].

## Icepick: AI Agent Library

Hatchet offers **Icepick**, a separate TypeScript library for building AI agents
on top of Hatchet's durable task queue [17][27].

| Attribute | Value | Source |
|-----------|-------|--------|
| Name | Icepick | [17] |
| Language | TypeScript only | [17] |
| Relationship | Built on Hatchet; uses durable execution | [17] |
| Philosophy | "Not a framework" — agents are functions | [17] |
| Repository | github.com/hatchet-dev/icepick | [27] |

Three core concepts [17]:

1. **Agents**: Functions calling other tools and agents
2. **Toolbox**: Collections of tools with AI-powered selection
3. **Tools**: Specific-task functions callable by agents

### Durable AI Execution

"Durable execution creates automatic checkpoints for agents so that they can
easily recover from failure or wait for external events" [17].

Claimed scale: "hundreds of thousands of tasks for a single execution" and
"billions of tasks per month" [17].

## LLM Response Streaming

Hatchet supports real-time streaming of LLM responses from workers to
consumers via `put_stream` [14]:

- Worker publishes stream chunks during task execution
- Consumer subscribes via `hatchet.runs.subscribe_to_stream(run_id)`
- Backend-as-proxy pattern recommended (e.g., FastAPI → SSE to frontend)
- Critical limitation: consumer must subscribe before events are published [14]

## MCP (Model Context Protocol) Support

The stale internal sheet listed MCP Integration as "Yes" — this requires
qualification.

### What Exists

1. **Documentation MCP server**: Hatchet provides an MCP endpoint at
   `https://docs.hatchet.run/api/mcp` allowing AI coding assistants (Cursor,
   Claude Code) to query Hatchet documentation [discovery agent findings].

2. **Job monitoring MCP server**: A separate MCP server exists for debugging
   and monitoring Hatchet jobs — list workflows, show failed runs, query by
   metadata, get queue metrics. Requires `HATCHET_CLIENT_TOKEN` [29].

3. **Third-party MCP server**: LobeHub lists a community "Hatchet MCP Server"
   (gjakobi-hatchet-mcp) for job monitoring [29].

### What Does NOT Exist

No evidence found that Hatchet workflows can **invoke** MCP tools at runtime.
MCP integration is for AI assistants interacting with Hatchet (documentation
and monitoring), not for workflows calling MCP servers as steps.

This is fundamentally different from n8n's MCP integration, which provides
bidirectional MCP support (n8n as both MCP client and server within
workflows).

## Native LLM Nodes

Hatchet has **no native LLM nodes** [1][17]. There are no built-in nodes for
calling OpenAI, Anthropic, or other LLM providers. AI integration is achieved
by writing code that calls LLM APIs within task functions — "just run a script
that calls an LLM."

Example from discovery agent: Hatchet examples show OpenAI usage with Langfuse
wrapper for observability, but this is user code, not platform-native.

## Comparison to n8n's AI Capabilities

| Feature | Hatchet | n8n |
|---------|---------|-----|
| Native LLM nodes | None | 70+ LangChain-integrated nodes |
| LLM providers | Via user code | 11 built-in (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, etc.) |
| RAG support | Via user code | 12 vector store backends built-in |
| Agent memory | Via user code | 8 memory backends (Postgres, Redis, etc.) |
| MCP support | Docs/monitoring only | Bidirectional (client + server) |
| AI templates | Limited examples | 6,137 AI-specific workflow templates |
| Streaming | put_stream method | Built into AI nodes |

## Gaps and Limitations

- **No native AI features** — AI is a use case, not a built-in capability
- **Icepick is TypeScript-only** — Python/Go users don't get the AI agent library
- **MCP is monitoring-only** — no runtime MCP tool calling from workflows
- **No Anthropic/Claude-specific integration** found in any source
- **No LangChain integration** — unlike n8n's deep LangChain embedding
- **Stream consumer race condition** — must subscribe before events publish [14]
